title: 1 Chronicles 20:4–8
context: A brief record of wars with the Philistines in which David's servants kill descendants of "the giant": Sibbecai kills Sippai, Elhanan kills Lahmi the brother of Goliath, and Jonathan son of Shimea kills a man with six fingers and toes on each hand and foot. This parallels 2 Samuel 21:18–22, with differences in places and names, and the Chronicler does not include the account of Ishbibenob and Abishai rescuing David (2 Samuel 21:15–17).

verses.text: After this, war arose at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they were subdued.
verses.arminianNotes: War arises at Gezer, and Sibbecai kills Sippai, "of the sons of the giant." Arminian readers note that the victories now come through David's servants, showing faithful men sharing in God's work.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that 2 Samuel 21:18 places this war at Gob and names the giant Saph. The Chronicler's place and name are recorded alongside the Samuel account without resolving the difference.

verses.text: Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
verses.arminianNotes: Elhanan son of Jair kills "Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite." Arminian readers note, consistent with the notes on 2 Samuel 21:19, that the WEB’s Samuel parallel also speaks of Goliath the Gittite’s brother but names Elhanan’s father Jaare-Oregim and does not give the brother’s name; the traditional Hebrew of 2 Samuel 21:19 lacks “brother.”
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise acknowledge the well-known difficulty in relating these verses to 1 Samuel 17 and 2 Samuel 21:19. Proposals offered there are held as proposals, and these notes declare no winner.

verses.text: There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot; and he also was born to the giant.
verses.arminianNotes: At Gath there is a man with twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and foot, also "born to the giant." Arminian readers note that the Chronicler records the detail plainly, as 2 Samuel 21:20 does.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the near-identical parallel in 2 Samuel 21:20. The unusual stature and features underline the strength of Israel's enemies and the greatness of the deliverance God gave.

verses.text: When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea, David’s brother, killed him.
verses.arminianNotes: When he defies Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, kills him. Arminian readers note that 2 Samuel 21:21 spells the name Shimei; the difference in spelling is noted without resolving it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the language of defying Israel echoes Goliath in 1 Samuel 17. Once again a member of David's family answers the challenge, and God gives his people victory.

verses.text: These were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.arminianNotes: "These were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants." Arminian readers note that 2 Samuel 21:22 says "these four," while Chronicles lists three, having omitted Ishbibenob.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the summary credits the victories to David and his servants together. God's establishment of David's kingdom is shared by those who serve under him.
